troubleshooting.title: The Git Client Reports a Filesystem Name Collision
troubleshooting.shortdesc: Tracked files whose names differ only in case or accent collide on your file system, so the Git Client flags them and blocks risky operations.

condition.title: Problem
condition.p: A Filesystem name collision warning appears in the view, and one or more files in the area are marked with a Path Collision icon. You cannot stage or discard those files, and stashing (along with the pull and pre-push operations that stash internally) is refused.

cause.title: Cause
cause.p: Two files tracked in the repository have names that differ only in letter case or Unicode form (for example, an accented and an unaccented spelling of the same name). On a case-insensitive or Unicode-folding file system (such as macOS APFS or Windows), both names resolve to a single physical file, so the two entries cannot be represented safely. Round-tripping them through a stash would delete the file, so the Git Client refuses those operations until you resolve the collision.

step.cmd: Decide which of the two colliding names to keep.

info.p: Because both names map to the same file on this file system, the Git Client cannot stage or discard them for you. Resolve the collision with command-line Git.

step.cmd: From a command line in the repository, remove the other name from Git without deleting the file on disk.

info.note: Alternatively, open the repository on a case-sensitive file system, where the two files are distinct, and rename or delete one of them there.

stepresult.p: Only one entry remains, so the warning clears and the held operations become available again.
